newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Country Road half yr profit slumps.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Country Road half yr profit slumps.

text.p: NOTE: Country Road Ltd is an apparel retailing group.

It said significant opportunites had been identified in these international markets. "Over the next 12 months we will commence to explore these opportunities to determine their feasibility and priority," Country Road chief executive Mike Howell said in a statement.
The outlook in the United States continued to be encouraging with a good response to the new season's merchandise, the company said.
Country Road earlier on Thursday announced a sharp fall in net profit in the six months to February 2, with difficult trading conditions in Australasia and losses in the U.S.
The U.S. operation, which is 25 percent owned by Itochu Corp of Japan, reduced its loss in the latest six months to A$300,000 from A$1.6 million a year ago.
Howell said Country Road now had two stores in Japan and expected that 25 to 30 outlets would be opened in the next five years in conjunction with Itochu.
The company was pleased with its Asian strategy.

"As part of our agreed business strategy with our partner, Inchcape, new store sites are being planned in Singapore, Hong Kong and Indonesia. We also expect to open our first store in Malaysia by the end of the year," Howell said.

Net profit slumped to A$1.09 million from A$5.53 million, with the latest result including an abnormal loss of A$3.05 million due to streamlining of operations and changes in the international development policy.

Net profit before abnormals was A$3.04 million. Howell said this was 45 percent below the year-ago period but was better than the January forecast that earnings could be more than 50 percent lower. Dividend was cut by 2.5 cents to 2.0 cents.
Sales fell to A$136.96 million from A$146.40 million, with sales in Australia and New Zealand falling 8.2 percent but U.S. sales rose 12.5 percent.
